name: Kellen Moore

views.text: An offense is a set of systems; keep what already works for these players and change the rest as they learn it.
If a play makes sense to the players, it stays in; if a player brings a good idea, it can go in the game plan.
A young quarterback earns the job by getting better every week; once he has it, build the plan around what he does well.
When a short-yardage call fails, the play-caller owns not putting the offense in the right spot.
A losing first season is a foundation if the young players got better; the record still was not good enough.
Hire people you already trust, let them be their best, and make play-calling a staff effort.
The offseason is for patience and evaluation, not for promises.
Smart, fast and physical beats any signature style.

signatures: keeps the same even expression on the sideline whether the offense is rolling or stalling
credits players for ideas that turned into big plays
answers questions about the future with a short, calm line about patience

motivation.want: to build a contender around a young quarterback he developed
motivation.fear: that a patient rebuild reads as a coach in over his head

want.text: a contender in New Orleans built around Tyler Shough

voice: Calm, quiet and precise; he answers in short, practical sentences without boasts. He talks about systems, development and staff collaboration, shares blame readily, and praises players for their growth and input. He rarely shows emotion in public and counsels patience when asked about the future.

evidence.summary: In his first Eagles spring he describes offenses as systems each coach approaches his own way, plans to keep what works and adjust as players learn, wants consistent terminology for fast execution, keeps plays that make sense to players, and will focus on the run game and play action in camp. His plan before any games.

Before Super Bowl LIX: Barkley calls him brilliant and open to player input, cites two playoff runs that came from his own suggestions, and says Moore's sideline demeanor never changes. Hurts values his fresh perspective. Doug Nussmeier, who followed him through three jobs, calls him smart, a strong communicator who weighs suggestions and adapts to personnel, and ready to lead. Fangio praises his run-pass balance. Colleagues' praise as he was about to leave.

Team announcement that Dallas and Moore mutually agreed to part ways with a year left on his deal, after McCarthy declined to guarantee his return. McCarthy's statement credits Moore's offensive production and his mentorship of Prescott. McCarthy then took over play-calling. Read through search summaries of the release; no Moore comment.

After a failed fourth-and-1, Moore takes blame alongside Sirianni, saying it was on him to put the offense in the right spot. He describes a collaborative staff with Sirianni heavily involved and calls the process excellent and similar to his earlier stops.

Introduced as the Saints' 19th head coach at 36, the league's youngest, after the Eagles' Super Bowl win; he will call the offensive plays himself, wants a smart, fast, physical team fans can rally behind and an environment where every player, coach and staffer can be his best, says everyone will be evaluated, sets no deadline for hiring coordinators and believes the team can compete right away. Team site.

His staff takes shape: Brandon Staley, who hired Moore as Chargers coordinator in 2023, becomes defensive coordinator, and Eagles quarterbacks coach Doug Nussmeier, from his Dallas, Chargers and Philadelphia staffs, is expected as offensive coordinator. Shows he hired people he already knew. Facts only.

Staley says he believes in Moore as much as anyone he has worked with, praising his flexibility and teaching and calling him a winner; Moore hired Staley partly for his versatility. Staley's view of Moore. Team site.

End of a 6-11 first season: upbeat and appreciative but measured, he says the team feels great about rookie Tyler Shough as the starter after he improved a great deal, explains that Spencer Rattler earned the early starts, admits the team did not win enough and must improve in all three phases, and counsels patience in the offseason. Loomis praises the staff for the late defensive improvement.
